cases.assertion: Have a stand-in capture argv and compare it with the exact configured strings, including an empty string, combined with per-launch arguments in the documented order.
Launch a stand-in using the compatibility command field and verify that specifying command and program together refuses that entry with the expected conflict.
Verify the configured effort reaches the stand-in and an explicit per-launch value wins. Check blank or unsupported effort choices fail with a field error.
Toggle enabled and verify the CLI catalog and start or resume behavior reflect the new value while unrelated entries remain usable.
Observe a stand-in's environment after configuration expansion and verify a string override, a null removal and a missing-reference refusal without exposing private values.
Read the CLI catalog and check an explicit valid entry icon and the default icon, then verify an invalid icon reports the specific entry field.
Verify the configured model reaches the stand-in and an explicit per-launch value wins. Check blank or unsupported model choices fail with a field error.
Launch an isolated stand-in from the configured program name or path and verify the intended executable runs. Verify a missing custom program reports the entry's problem.
Add an entry with a built-in or custom type, verify the expected invocation rules, and refuse a missing type or a built-in entry that changes its type.

Use two temporary absolute homes with different settings and verify each launch sees only its own settings and agents. Confirm an empty override uses the temporary user home and a relative override is refused.

Start a fake CLI with a missing or comments-only file and verify defaults. Verify JSONC comments and trailing commas are accepted and malformed or duplicate keys give source locations and refuse any launch before a process or worktree exists.
Configure an added CLI and a bad entry; verify the valid entry's advertised type and actual launch and verify the bad entry refuses only its own starts with a field location.
Start an unnamed fake CLI with a controlled name pool, verify trimming, unused and exhausted pool selection, and verify an empty pool uses the Framework built-in names.
Read a settings file with a string $schema and verify the effective launch settings are unchanged. A non-string $schema reports its location and blocks starts.
Run a fake CLI before and after changing yolo; verify each start and resume reads the current value, an existing run keeps its captured policy and a Guest captures its value on first tool use.
Observe a real agent or terminal mutation as an id-less changed frame tagged with its owning connection's watch ID and read the expected payload.
Observe an id-less closing announcement naming the replacement build during a live takeover, and reconnect with the same running agent still reachable.
Deny a foreground handoff and observe a connect_failed frame with the reason, no connected notification and no recorded successful connection.
Observe the id-less foreground handoff notification with the authenticated peer identity and verify the roster shows its connected state.
Lose a live forwarded subscription and observe the daemon's watch_ended carrying the former local watch ID and reason, then establish a fresh watch.
Send raw input and resize as id-less calls with exact permissions and target. Observe the expected input bytes and resized view, and verify no JSON-RPC response is written for either notification.
Send an id-less cancel naming a pending send. Observe the cancelled original request before paste, no target input, and no separate notification response.
Acknowledge takeover with an id-less empty closing frame; verify the old stream ends and a fresh attachment reaches the same surviving CLI.
Call a known operation after hello and correlate its ID and typed result with the target. Verify malformed or unknown operations return an error for the same ID.
Cancel a pending agent.send request on the same connection; correlate the cancellation acknowledgement and original settlement and verify no recipient input occurred before paste.

Send a v1 offer over the isolated daemon socket as terminal and IDE clients. Verify the response ID, negotiated v1, build, machine ID, service PIDs, agent count and each client's advertised operations and topics. Refuse a second hello on the same connection.
Release an owned watch and receive a matching acknowledgement. Perform a fresh mutation and confirm the closed watch receives no further changes.
Subscribe after hello and verify the correct snapshot followed by the matching watch ID on a mutation's live update.
Send id-less topology on an authenticated machine link, verify the receiving roster learns the route, and observe a subsequent remote call use it without an advertisement response.
Cancel a pending forwarded send with an id-less peer notification; observe the original settlement and unchanged recipient input before paste, with no separate response.
Observe an authenticated peer's id-less changed frame mapped to the matching local watch and verify the payload came from the expected remote agent.
Observe an authenticated peer's idle shutdown report the correct machine as sleeping, leaving other peers unchanged and ordinary roster queries passive.
Observe the peer's id-less watch_ended for the forwarded subscription and verify the owning local watch closes with the corresponding reason.
Advertise topology with a request ID over an authenticated link, verify the correlated response and observe a subsequent call taking the advertised route.
Cancel a still-pending forwarded send by its peer-side request ID and check the acknowledgement and original settlement with no paste or second delivery.
Forward a call or watch on an authenticated peer link. Verify only the intended remote run receives the effect and the peer response or watch snapshot correlates with the original ID.
Send a machine hello over an authenticated isolated peer connection; verify v1 negotiation and peer identity, then reject an invalid offer or mismatched machine identity before admitting it.
Send an authenticated peer unwatch for its own remote subscription, observe the acknowledged remote ID, and verify the former watch ceases delivering output.
Return the exact agent identity, state and current attachments.
Return the expected live identities and visible Guests without exposing unauthorized records.
Remove a selected live agent and observe exit and removal for that Agent reference while unrelated agents stay available.
Read back the new name under the original reference.
Resume an exact saved session through the daemon and verify the same Agent reference when reusing its record, with the expected new process and working folder.
Read a stopped agent or saved session as a resumable candidate; assert its identity, CLI, folder and requested machine scope.
Read known logical lines and verify the requested bound.
Correlate the delivery receipt and verify a single delivery at the intended target after reconnect and replay with the original request ID.
Start a fake CLI with a chosen folder and request ID, read back the resulting stable address and location, and submit the same request ID twice to ensure only one process exists.
Correlate each requested target with a receipt and an observed stopped or refused state.
Observe exact text or key bytes on the intended terminal. Check partial input is distinguishable from full input.
Resize an owned watch and observe the shared screen adopt the expected dimensions, with a different connection's attempt rejected.
Discover the configured test CLI and verify its advertised capability on the requested machine.
Read known daemon log text with the requested line and byte bounds as a terminal client; confirm an agent caller is refused.
Read the expected daemon and Keeper identity, build and state.
Complete a compatible takeover while retaining the same Keeper and CLI; verify disjoint Daemon or Keeper offers are refused without replacing the installed build.
Read expected visible agent records from their holder across an authenticated peer link; check that the same operation is unavailable on an ordinary local client connection.
Resize a forwarded Attach view through its holder and observe the correct remote watch and terminal apply the new dimensions.
Observe the authenticated peer call returning the exact original Shell request ID, replying AgentRef, distinct message references and full reply text. Reconcile the peer acknowledgement.
Observe one authenticated background delivery failure with the original qualified message and target. Replaying the admitted send preserves its single notice.
Read the remote start outcome at the requester and correlate the receipt and exact Agent reference with the single remote process started.
Have a remote child wait for the person and verify its creator receives a single notice naming that child and its wait kind. Refuse a notice from the wrong machine without posting it.
Use the saved route between isolated peers, observe that the required intermediate link opens, and verify the subsequent operation reaches the intended machine.
Read the holder's resumable records through the authenticated peer route; verify exact saved session identity, with no local-client access.
Return the expected local or remote workspace locations and their kinds.
Authorize one foreground handoff to a known isolated peer and verify the resulting machine ID and roster state for the connection lifecycle.
Return the local roster with the expected peer and route state for this caller.
Remove the expected saved connection and observe the roster change with other routes intact.
Rename a remote peer through the allowed session and read its new name under the same machine ID.
Send an invalid request and verify a JSON-RPC error code, typed reason and the expected response ID, with no result or requested effect.
Receive a successful typed result over the daemon socket and verify its JSON-RPC version, original request ID and payload with no error member.
Subscribe and verify the initial visible-agent snapshot, the second agent's exact update and end state, and no updates after unwatch.
Read the selected agent's screen snapshot and verify later output and an exit refer to the same watch and terminal.

Open the selected agent's dedicated watch on a fresh Terminal connection. Refuse an IDE or previously used Terminal connection. Verify that exit closes the unread transport and both services exit naturally.
Read the roster snapshot and observe a subsequent matching peer and connection-state update on that watch.
Receive an id-less Keeper exit frame and match its Agent ID and process exit evidence to the fake CLI that ended.
Send a typed keeper operation and correlate the response ID, result and any transferred terminal with the intended fake CLI.
Authenticate the fixture daemon, negotiate Keeper v1 independently and verify held agent IDs, PIDs and birth values. Refuse a process that is not the authorized daemon.
On Windows receive duplicated terminal handles in the start result and use them for I/O with the new CLI whose identity was returned.
On Windows hand the Keeper a live CLI's duplicated terminal handles in an agent.sync request and verify it adopts and observes the same process.
On Windows reacquire the held CLI's terminal handles from the Keeper's agent.sync response and use them for I/O with the unchanged process.
Start a fake CLI as the authenticated daemon, compare the returned PID and birth identity and prove the received PTY or ConPTY is the new CLI's terminal.
Request stop by Keeper agent ID and verify the terminal process ends, the same ID is reported in the exit frame and unrelated terminal processes stay held.
Transfer a live terminal to the side that lacks it and verify the same PID and birth remain usable after sync. Reject conflicting identity before changing ownership.
Use the authenticated Daemon-Keeper link to verify heartbeat acknowledgement and monitor survival while heartbeats continue and watchdog replacement when they stop.
Send an invalid or refused Keeper call and verify its correlated typed error and unchanged terminal ownership.
Receive a correlated Keeper success response whose required result fields and native resources match the selected operation.
Cancel a pending send over the relay using its requestId; verify the cancelled response and confirm nothing was typed or retained for later delivery.
Send the id-less initialized notification over stdio after initialize, then verify there is no notification response and the next request gets its own correlated result.
Send initialize through the real relay and verify correlated protocol version, server identity, capabilities and instructions.
Send ping through the real relay and verify the same request ID receives an empty result.
Make a real stdio call and verify JSON-RPC ID, the MCP structured content and the targeted Framework effect, including a reasoned tool refusal.
Read the real relay's tool list and compare tool names and input schemas with the active Framework registry for the managed or Guest connection.
Read the expected agent addresses and related state under a managed actor and a Guest; verify a YOLO-off caller cannot see agents outside its creation tree.

Send a 100-key batch containing Unicode as a JSON string and single Esc and Enter keys through the real relay. Reject empty, oversized and malformed batches and confirm the CLI received only the accepted exact bytes.
Verify the owning Guest reads the complete correlated reply and can find its retained record by the original address. The unread list clears and a different Guest cannot fetch or settle that reply.
Read known logical terminal lines inline for the selected managed target and verify a Guest target is refused because it has no terminal.

Correlate the original full receipt with complete delivery to the intended managed terminal through Guest MCP. An explicit read wait uses that message ID and accepts only a linked reply, and the send offers no implicit next call.
Create exactly one managed child from the caller's desired folder and CLI environment and compare the returned address with the actual new run.
Stop only the selected managed agent, verify its exit or the documented termination-unconfirmed result, and confirm its unrelated helpers stay live.
Observe the exact text and optional Enter in the target's fake terminal; verify the tool reports what it typed and cannot type to a Guest target.
A foreground start preserves native titles and alternate screen output. Detach restores the original shell page, scrollback and input mode while the exact agent stays running.
Detach restores the caller terminal and a second Attach reaches the same live run.
A foreground Attach returns the selected child exit status.
Attach to one agent and read live terminal output for that process.
An authenticated agent start confirms a recognized Claude trust choice once when the target home enables YOLO. YOLO off and an unrecognized choice do not confirm trust.
An authorized caller can operate on the selected agent and see its own result.
A refused request preserves relevant files, agents, routes and inboxes.
A Claude start by a person in Shell or VS Code leaves its folder trust prompt pending with YOLO enabled. Only the person's explicit Down and Enter reach the fake CLI.
Reject a mismatched machine identity and disambiguate equal agent names on different machines.
A Guest receives exactly one reply over MCP correlated to the original request.
A Guest receives the first linked reply under a result wait. On reply timeout, a filtered read with the same original message ID gets the eventual reply without sending the request again.
A second caller cannot fetch the original Guest’s reply.
New terminal input cancels the pending probe and a draft-safe send leaves the person’s draft intact.
A rejected key batch leaves the target input untouched.
Send mixed text and keys through Shell and the wire. Observe all steps in order on the terminal before later raw input, and reject invalid Shell spellings before input.
The fake CLI observes the intended Unicode and key sequence in order.
An invalid archive digest or incompatible target leaves the installed programs and state usable.
Install the candidate archive on the native target and use its program to start and query a fake CLI.
Upgrade the pinned prior installation using the candidate archive and verify the promised state and program identity.
By default Shell reports the exact inbox receipt while a draft still blocks delivery. After clearing it, the explicit delivery wait returns a distinct receipt and each message is submitted once.
One target receives the intended body, sender identity and receipt correlation.
Drop the reply after delivery and retry the original request ID. The result settles once with one delivery.
Zero-budget MCP sends return accepted inbox IDs while a draft blocks delivery, and a read returns exactly those messages. Invalid waits allocate no message.
Disconnect during raw input and verify the returned partial or unknown outcome matches the effect observed at the target.
Shell waits for the original remote recipient’s linked reply and writes the exact multiline reply to stdout. The remote fake CLI sees one request and the origin sees no terminal input.
Replace a pinned compatible v1 build in place, preserve the live PID and resume its interaction.
An offer with no compatible version is refused before program or state changes.
Use actual SSH transport to a disposable peer and observe the selected machine and corresponding agent effect.
Discover the selected remote machine, create the worktree from its HEAD and observe the same CLI from Shell and Extension. The local repository stays intact.
Lose the cross-machine reply after delivery. A retry with the original ID observes the same settlement and one delivery.
Route loss is visible and the route can recover to the original agent identity.
Resolve an unqualified agent selector across a disconnected saved route, check literal names containing @ and ambiguity, and verify automatic name allocation does not probe that route.
Replace the Daemon while a Keeper owns the process. Observe the original CLI identity, reattach and read its output.
Exercise the supported failure and recovery path for Keeper and verify terminal ownership and process cleanup.
Recover a pending effect after service replacement and reconcile one settlement with one observed effect.
A failed launch publishes no agent record and leaves no live process.
Launch each managed built-in beside the person's existing Facade MCP entry and verify the run gets Facade's tools without the retired skill.
Show current Claude and Pi session labels in running and resumable lists, including renamed and unnamed sessions. Resume the same saved session using its original full ID.
Retry a start with the original request ID after losing the reply and observe one run.
Start the selected CLI in the requested folder and resolve the returned stable identity to that same process.
Stop the selected targets and check each result and the unaffected agent.
Request both explicit model and effort through MCP for OpenCode and verify the combined refusal leaves no child agent.
Reconnect obtains the current snapshot and discards stale events from the previous connection.
Watch returns the initial snapshot and a later correlated update for the chosen subject.
Unwatch releases its watch and ends updates for its subscription while other subscriptions continue.
Observe the installed relay acknowledge the daemon's closing notice with empty params, then complete a pending MCP call across replacement without duplicating its effect.
Launch the installed relay for a known fake run, verify the daemon admits its local identity and observe a reconnect hello using the existing run after replacement.
Connect the installed relay to the isolated daemon and verify the matching hello result selects the relay contract before MCP input is served.
Attach to the intended process, observe its output and detach with that process still alive.
Start a fake CLI and check Shell prints the expected stable address, name and state in the selected machine scope.
Run the machine command group without a subcommand; verify scoped help, exit zero and no daemon startup.
Register the authenticated peer and read back the persisted machine identity and route.
Connect to a controlled peer in the foreground, verify its identity and keep both daemons alive until the connection closes.
Assert the roster shows the expected peer identity and connection state.
Remove the saved peer by exact ID and verify that peer's saved route disappears while another matching name stays intact.
Read the changed peer name from the roster under the original machine ID.
Read the changed name back through the same stable reference.
Resume the exact saved session and verify the new process and folder. Assert the listing route with no reference.
Write known multiline output to a fake CLI and verify stdout shows the last requested logical lines, with invalid counts rejected before opening services.
Correlate the CLI receipt with a single delivery to the intended recipient.
Launch the requested fake CLI in the selected folder and read back its stable address, effective argv and running process.
Read state and identity for the selected live agent and the daemon-only status when no target is given. An empty home stays idle.
Stop the selected process and assert the per-target receipt and final state.
Observe the exact input bytes and the requested Enter behavior at the target.
Select an explicit version through the controlled installer fixture and check that Shell uses and reports the matching asset receipt.
Resume the given saved session with -d, verify the original agent address and a new running process, and check the CLI received the saved session ID.
Resume the given saved session on an isolated terminal, observe the resumed process's output and check Ctrl+] detaches while that process continues.
Start the fake CLI with -d, verify stdout names its stable address and check the process is alive after the launcher exits zero.
Start the fake CLI on an isolated terminal, observe its output and verify that the foreground command returns the child's exit status.
Compare root and scoped help output with the expected help pages for both help spellings and check that no Facade services start.
Compare the supported version flag outputs with the build version and verify that no Facade services start.
Launch the isolated daemon and negotiate over its socket. Exercise takeover with a test build.
Launch the installed relay with the fake CLI's private configuration, verify it serves that run over stdio, then close input and observe pending replies and successful exit.
Check the approval hook emits approval for Facade's own recognized tools and leaves unrelated tool requests undecided.
Send the CLI hook request and check its formatted response delivers the agent's saved instructions and folder context to the matching run.
Supply a fake session-start payload, verify the session and optional skill output for the current run, and check that a background job posts no session.
Run the title hook with fixture input; verify the saved conversation and that only the configured title command's stdout reaches the CLI after it receives the original input.
Start through the installed launcher and prove the Keeper owns the test CLI terminal.
Start the background SSH link in an isolated home and verify the command returns with the expected saved peer and the link still carrying requests.
Pass an authenticated machine hello over the process's stdio and verify malformed or incompatible offers are refused before opening the daemon or changing running agents.
Exercise SSH administration in two isolated homes and verify that only the paired authorization is installed or removed, including refusal for a mismatched peer.

cases.assertion: After a legacy handover record exists, read the derived predecessor instance for this editor session and verify Framework uses it to retain the workspace. A fresh window must not invent a predecessor.
Read version 1 and the current session and stable handover token from the live component. An earlier editor session receives no identity.
Register an actual terminal with the current claim using begin and finish. Verify a ticket is bound to this run and session and that a stale finish leaves the live terminal untouched.
Activate a newer session-matched claim and observe that the previous activation loses authority to replace the current terminal. Reject a conflicting token at the same generation.

test.name: Window terminal registration: actual objects across workspace host generations old activation, late finish and late cancel cannot replace or clear a newer capture

cases.assertion: Begin registration for the chosen run. Verify a nonempty ticket is scoped to its owner and only one terminal capture is active at once.

test.name: Window terminal registration: actual objects across workspace host generations one nonempty capture ticket belongs to its session, owner and run

cases.assertion: Cancel a pending capture, verify its ticket can no longer bind a terminal, and show the next registration succeeds without disposing the old terminal.

test.name: Window terminal registration: actual objects across workspace host generations expired and cancelled captures dispose nothing, and release the next creation

cases.assertion: Use the matching ticket to bind the exact current Terminal object. A stale ticket or ambiguous set of candidate objects preserves the existing binding.

cases.assertion: Write a newline-framed request on the live socket. Verify its sender, operation, arguments and remaining deadline reach the intended peer exactly once.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a route reaches the other window's component with who asked, what and how long it has, and brings back its answer

cases.assertion: Send concurrent requests and complete their peer operations in reverse order. Each JSON reply ID resolves only its original request and an unmatched reply changes neither.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) live socket replies match concurrent calls by ID in reverse completion order and ignore an unmatched ID

cases.assertion: Route an agent list query and verify the receiving window returns its own locations, CLI availability and caller-visible agent identities.

test.name: Journey: an agent works with an agent of another window on this computer (J15, M01, M03, COLLABORATION-1.1) it lists the other window, starts an agent there, messages it, reads its screen and stops it

cases.assertion: Route a tool call between legacy windows. Verify the receiving window evaluates reach, acts on its own exact target and returns the correlated result for the originating caller.

test.name: Journey: an agent works with an agent of another window on this computer (J15, M01, M03, COLLABORATION-1.1) the actual Window Component routes to the exact peer and refuses stale sessions and malformed calls

cases.assertion: Route a message to a peer-owned agent. Correlate sender, recipient, original message ID and reply reference with one complete message in the intended fake terminal.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a peer send preserves its exact sender, recipient, message and reply, and a result returns once to the sender copy over live sockets (RULES-1.1, 1.7)

cases.assertion: Route a delivery result back to its originating agent and verify one receipt with the original call or request ID updates the sender copy.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a peer send preserves its exact sender, recipient, message and reply, and a result returns once to the sender copy over live sockets (RULES-1.1, 1.7)

cases.assertion: Cause the remote handler to throw after dispatch and verify the correlated failed reply reports effects unknown. A request missing required fields reports failed with effects none and runs no handler.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a request in another protocol, or incomplete, is answered with why and serves nothing

cases.assertion: Send a correlated request with a different network protocol directly to the socket. Verify protocol_incompatible with effects none and zero handler calls.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a request in another protocol, or incomplete, is answered with why and serves nothing

cases.assertion: Verify an expired request is rejected before dispatch with effects none. For a sent request whose reply is late, observe timeout with effects unknown and discard the late reply.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a request answered later than its deadline times out, its effects unknown; the late answer goes nowhere

cases.assertion: Disconnect a peer with an in-flight request and observe window_unavailable with effects unknown. Verify a new request to a peer absent from the directory reports effects none.

test.name: Window network: window components register and carry requests between windows (ARCHITECTURE-1.1, 2.1) a request under way when the other window goes may have acted there: unavailable, its effects unknown
